atoms.b: Ancient Greek houses were designed to stay cool in the ((++hot freezing)) Greek weather.
They had a courtyard in the middle and ((++wooden glass)) shutters on the windows to block out the sun.
The walls were made of ((++mud metal)) bricks, which is why most houses didn’t survive until today.

instruction.text: Which material might the Greeks have used for the base of their homes?

text: These sturdy, stone foundations have survived and teach us a lot about the layout of houses in ancient Greece.

atoms.a: In ancient Greece, was bathing considered a public or private activity?
Who do you think had the luxury of bathing privately?

feedback.end: Wealthy women could ask enslaved people to bring them hot water for bathing at home.

atoms.b: The courtyard was a shared space where both men and women gathered to ((++socialise watch_TV)). However, other areas of the houses were more divided.
The women’s quarters, called the gynaeceum, were private and used for tasks like ((++weaving wrestling)) and childcare.
The men’s area, known as the andron, was a public space for male guests and had mosaic floors with ((++beautiful ugly)) art to impress visitors.
